## Step 1

**🧠 PM reasoning:**

> Verrica is a commercial-stage dermatology company with YCANTH approved for molluscum contagiosum in July 2023. They reported FY2025 revenue of $35.6M, with their fiscal year ending December 31, 2025, though I'm working through the exact quarterly breakdown to confirm the reporting periods.
> 
> Looking at the quarterly revenue pattern: Q1 2025 appears to be around $3.4M, Q2 2025 $12.7M, Q3 2025 $14.3M, Q4 2025 $5.1M, and Q1 2026 $5.0M. The significant spike in Q2-Q3 2025 likely reflects Torii milestone payments or channel inventory stocking, followed by a notable decline in Q4. What's striking is their debt situation—they carried $35.7M in debt (an OrbiMed loan) through Q3 2025 but paid it down to just $1.6M by Q4 2025, suggesting they used some of that Q3 revenue surge to substantially reduce their debt burden.
> 
> The balance sheet shift is dramatic: equity swung from negative $17M in Q3 to positive $24.7M in Q4 2025, indicating a major recapitalization event. Looking at the paid-in capital, it jumped roughly $50M from Q3 to Q4, which combined with the debt payoff suggests they raised significant equity capital and used it to deleverage. The share count increased modestly from 9.49M to 10.65M shares, which seems inconsistent with a $50M raise unless the pricing was quite high or there's something else going on with the capital structure. I need to verify whether there was a reverse split involved, since the historical share counts are unusually low for a company of this size. There's also litigation to track—Rosen and Schall investigations initiated in March.
> 
> Now I'm looking at the business fundamentals. Verrica is a hybrid commercial and clinical-stage dermatology company. YCANTH is their approved molluscum product generating real revenue with strong unit growth, while they're also running Phase 3 trials for common warts and have VP-315, an oncolytic peptide for basal cell carcinoma showing promising abscopal effects in Phase 2. The valuation really hinges on a sum-of-the-parts approach: the commercial ramp of YCANTH, the probability-weighted value of the Phase 3 common warts program, the BCC opportunity with VP-315, plus some smaller royalty upside from their Torii partnership in Japan. To properly model this, I need to nail down the actual share count including any dilution from warrants and options, understand the recapitalization details from Q4, and get clarity on YCANTH's net revenue economics.
> 
> I'm going to split this analysis across a few angles in parallel: one track on the commercial and financial story including capital structure, another on the pipeline science and mechanism of action for VP-315, and a third on the competitive landscape and market sizing for molluscum and common warts. I'll pull the full income statement, cash flow, segment data, peer comparisons, and any transcript or insider information to round out the picture.

**PM note:** This is a commercial-stage dermatology company (YCANTH/VP-102 approved for molluscum) with a clinical pipeline (common warts Phase 3, VP-315 oncolytic peptide for basal cell carcinoma). I note a major Q4 2025 recapitalization (debt paid off, ≈$50M APIC increase) and securities-law investigations in March 2026. Let me pull more and spawn specialists.

# VRCA — Capital Structure & Cash Reconstruction (as of Q1 2026 10-Q, filed 5/12/2026; FY2025 10-K, filed 3/11/2026)

## BOTTOM LINE
FMP's "≈10.65M shares" is **wrong/stale** — it is neither the legal share count nor the weighted average. The reality: Verrica did a **1-for-10 reverse split effective at the close of July 24, 2025**, then issued a large November 2025 insider-anchored PIPE. **Actual shares outstanding = 17,178,786** (17,189,300 issued less 10,514 treasury) at both 12/31/25 and 3/31/26 [Q1-2026 10-Q, balance sheet]. On a fully-diluted economic basis (including 5.31M pre-funded warrants), the base is **≈22.5M shares**, and the Q1-2026 EPS denominator was **21,305,025** [Q1-2026 10-Q, statement of operations]. The Manning/Caligan/BKB Form 4s showing "millions of shares" are correct and **not** in conflict with the real count — they are post-split holdings. Funded debt is **zero** (OrbiMed fully extinguished Nov 2025); the "$1.6M debt" is entirely lease liabilities. Cash is **$20.6M** at 3/31/26, burning **≈$9–9.5M/quarter**, and the company itself carries a **going-concern (substantial doubt) qualification** — runway is roughly **2 quarters (cash-out ≈Q3/Q4 2026)**, which flatly contradicts management's November 2025 "runway into mid-2027" claim. That gap is the single most important red flag and is plausibly connected to the March 2026 investigations.

---

|---|---|---|
| **Reverse stock split** | **1-for-10**, effective close of trading **July 24, 2025**; all periods retroactively adjusted | Q1-2026 10-Q, Note 1 ("Reverse Stock Split") |
| Shares **issued** (3/31/26 & 12/31/25) | **17,189,300** | Q1-2026 10-Q balance sheet |
| Treasury shares | 10,514 | same |
| **Shares outstanding** | **17,178,786** | same |
| Common par / authorized | $0.0001 / 200,000,000 | same |
| Preferred | 10,000,000 auth; **0 issued/outstanding** | same |

| Q1-2025 weighted-avg (comparative) | 9,483,734 | same |

**Why FMP shows 10,652,367:** that figure ≈ the pre-PIPE share base and is mis-mapped; it is neither the 17.18M legal count nor the 21.3M weighted diluted count. Pre-split the company had ≈92.5M shares (→ ≈9.25M post-split); the Nov 2025 PIPE then roughly doubled the count. **There is no contradiction with the insider Form 4s** — Manning holds ≈4.1M post-split shares, Caligan holds millions; those are real and consistent with a 17.18M outstanding base.

## ASSET 1 — YCANTH (VP-102): cantharidin 0.7% for molluscum contagiosum (APPROVED)

### Mechanism: cantharidin as a vesicant
Cantharidin is a terpenoid toxin from blister beetles and a potent inhibitor of protein phosphatases 1 and 2A (PP1/PP2A), with ≈10× greater affinity for PP2A (research: pharmacology reviews; PP2A is the original "cantharidin-binding protein"). Its **dermatologic action**, however, runs through a protease cascade: cantharidin absorbs into the lipid layers of epidermal keratinocytes → activates **neutral serine proteases** → these degrade the **desmosomal dense plaque** → tonofilaments detach from desmosomes → **acantholysis** → an **intra-epidermal (suprabasal) blister** (research: Frontiers pharmacology review; ultrastructural acantholysis studies). Because injury is confined above the basal layer and does not reach the dermis, **lesions heal without scarring**. Cantharidin has **no direct antiviral effect** on the molluscum poxvirus; it works by physically lifting off virus-laden epidermis and recruiting a local inflammatory response (neutrophils at 24h, monocytes/macrophages 24–72h per the cantharidin blister model). Honest nuance: the *bridge* between PP2A inhibition and protease activation is the prevailing interpretation but is not definitively proven (research) — this is a decades-old, empirically reliable clinical effect even if the full molecular chain is incompletely mapped.

### Disease and population
Molluscum is a highly contagious poxvirus infection producing flesh-colored papules, typically 10–30 lesions (sometimes >100); untreated, lesions persist on average ≈13 months and up to 5 years (10-K FY2025, Item 1). ≈6M Americans affected, ≈1M diagnosed annually, 5–11% pediatric prevalence concentrated ages 1–14 (10-K FY2025, Item 1). **Before YCANTH there was no FDA-approved therapy.**

### Pivotal efficacy/safety (CAMP-1 & CAMP-2)
Two identical, vehicle-controlled Phase 3 trials, 528 patients ≥2 yrs, randomized 3:2, dosed every 21 days up to 4 applications; CAMP-1 ran under an FDA Special Protocol Assessment (JAMA Dermatol 2020;156(12):1315–1323, Eichenfield et al.):
- **Primary endpoint (complete clearance of all lesions, Day 84): CAMP-1 46% vs 18% vehicle; CAMP-2 54% vs 13% (both p<0.001).**
- Mean lesion-count reduction 69–83% (drug) vs ≈20% (vehicle); pooled 76% vs 0.3% (p<0.0001).
- **Safety**: AEs in 95–99% of treated patients, but **almost entirely mechanism-based local skin reactions** (application-site vesicles, pain, pruritus, erythema, scab). **No treatment-related serious AEs or deaths**; AE-driven discontinuation only ≈1.9%.

### Assessment
The mechanism is physical/pharmacodynamic and highly plausible; efficacy is statistically robust but ≈50% of patients do not fully clear in 12 weeks. The product's edge is **standardization** (GMP cantharidin >99% pure, fixed 0.7% concentration, single-use applicator) converting decades of unapproved compounded use into the first FDA-approved therapy with 5-year NCE exclusivity (10-K FY2025, Item 1). **PoS = 100%** — regulatory/technical risk is eliminated; remaining risk is commercial.

### Commercial reality (skeptical view)
The launch has been slow. Q1 FY2026 US YCANTH product revenue was just $4.3M (up 25% YoY), ≈15,300 dispensed applicators (Q1 FY2026 transcript) — an annualized run-rate of only ≈$17M, despite ≈250M covered lives and 40–45 reps. FY2025 total revenue of $35.6M was inflated by ≈$18M of one-time Torii milestones (10-K FY2025, Item 1; get_financials). Management's "$1B+ TAM" is aspirational. Japan launched Feb 2026 (Torii/Shionogi; royalty/transfer-price economics to Verrica), and an EU MAA filing is targeted ≈Q4 2026 on existing data (no new Phase 3 required) (Q3 FY2025 & Q1 FY2026 transcripts). **Realistic US peak ≈$80–130M** over 5–7 years if pull-through and reimbursement keep improving, plus modest royalty/transfer income from Japan and optional EU/ROW.

## PART 1 — THE US MOLLUSCUM MARKET AND YCANTH'S COMPETITIVE POSITION

### 1.1 Disease and market size — large, pediatric, self-limiting

Molluscum contagiosum (MC) is a benign, self-limited poxvirus skin infection spread by skin-to-skin contact, fomites, and autoinoculation. The most-cited US burden is **≈6 million Americans affected, mostly children** (Verrica commercial materials; a 2025 clinical paper states MC "affects 6 million people in the United States annually"). General-population prevalence is **≈5%**, with the highest incidence in children under 14 (Del Rosso et al., *J Clin Aesthet Dermatol* 2023); pediatric point prevalence runs **5.1–11.5%** (Olsen et al. meta-analysis, *Family Practice* 2014). Visit-based US incidence is ≈22 MC-associated outpatient visits per 10,000 persons/yr (Indian Health Service cohort), and the disease has been rising for decades (private-physician visits rose 11-fold 1966–1983).

**The structural governor on the market is spontaneous resolution.** CDC: papules "usually disappear spontaneously within 6 to 12 months… may take as long as 4 years." This is why the AAD and Cochrane endorse **watchful waiting / "benign neglect"** as first-line — and it is the single biggest reason the *treated, reimbursable* market is a fraction of the 6M prevalence headline. Any model that applies penetration to 6M overstates the opportunity; the correct denominator is the **physician-treated subset** (realistically ≈2.5–3M who present and elect active treatment).

### 1.2 Pre-YCANTH treatment landscape — a fragmented, off-label vacuum

Before YCANTH's July 2023 approval, **there was no FDA-approved drug for MC at all.** Care split across:
- **Watchful waiting** (free; exploits self-resolution; leaves contagion/cosmesis/psychosocial burden).
- **Compounded cantharidin ("beetle juice")** — the de facto standard, but unapproved since cantharidin lost FDA approval in 1962; cheap, entrenched, inconsistent concentration/stability. The 2006 Hanna RCT showed it often required 2–3 visits.
- **Cryotherapy** (liquid nitrogen) — painful, blistering, dyspigmentation risk; poorly suited to young children/numerous lesions (CDC).
- **Curettage** — effective but requires anesthesia and a cooperative patient; impractical for toddlers with high lesion counts; scarring risk (CDC explicitly cautions against scraping).
- **Imiquimod — proven ineffective** (two FDA pediatric RCTs, 702 children: ≈24–26% clearance vs. ≈26–28% vehicle); label updated 2007 to "failed to demonstrate efficacy."
- Oral cimetidine, KOH, salicylic acid, etc. — off-label, unproven.

### 1.3 YCANTH's competitive position

YCANTH (cantharidin 0.7%, formerly VP-102) is a **GMP drug-device combination** — a single-use applicator delivering a standardized, precise dose, administered **in-office every ≈3 weeks** for up to 4 treatments. Its differentiation versus the legacy landscape is fourfold:

## 1. Management & Board: a sponsor-installed team rebuilt on the ashes of a failed launch

**The pivotal fact about Verrica's leadership is that essentially the entire C-suite was replaced in late 2024 after the YCANTH launch failed, and the replacements were installed by — and largely drawn from — the controlling shareholder, PBM Capital.** This is simultaneously the bull case (aligned, financially committed sponsor took direct control and recapitalized the company) and the central governance risk (a non-independent, related-party-dominated structure).

### The launch failure that triggered the turnover
YCANTH (VP-102, GMP-controlled topical cantharidin delivered via single-use applicator) was approved by the FDA on **July 21, 2023** as the first and only approved therapy for molluscum contagiosum, and launched commercially in **September 2023** [FY2025 10-K, Item 1; Q1-2026 10-Q, Item 2]. The launch relied on a physician-administered "buy-and-bill" reimbursement model and an ≈80-territory field force, against which spending ballooned while uptake lagged: SG&A jumped to ≈$16.5M in Q2-2024 (from ≈$5.9M a year earlier), and Q3-2024 net product revenue actually went **negative** on a $1.7M product-returns provision. To fund the launch the company had taken on the **$50M OrbiMed term loan (July 2023)** with restrictive covenants that later forced early principal amortization and a going-concern qualification — the over-leverage that the November 2025 recapitalization was designed to undo.

In **October 2024** the company cut its sales territories from ≈80 to ≈35 and reduced its overall cost structure by ≈50%; in 2024 it cut headcount ≈29%, "including the transition of our former Chief Executive Officer, Chief Commercial Officer and Chief Financial Officer" [FY2025 10-K]. The turnover, chronologically:
- **CCO Joe Bonaccorso** resigned effective Aug 30, 2024 (seat then vacant/interim for ≈18 months).
- **CFO Terry Kohler** (joined July 2021) departed October 2024.
- **Founder-era CEO Ted White** — CEO since 2017, ex-President/GM of Almirall's medical-dermatology business — resigned effective **November 5, 2024** [8-K].

The sponsor's operator, installed to take direct control. |
